mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a robust demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average with no concurrent increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market expansion without slack, which supports wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) show a consistent quarterly growth above 3% for two consecutive quarters, indicating strong and persistent demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered quarters (t-test p > 0.05).
